# Additional tests for the fused layer norm kernel
def run_kernel(x, w, b, eps=1e-5):
    """Launch the kernel directly, returning output, mean, rstd."""
    M, N = x.shape
    y = torch.empty_like(x)
    mean = torch.empty((M,), dtype=torch.float32, device=x.device)
    rstd = torch.empty((M,), dtype=torch.float32, device=x.device)
    _layer_norm_fwd_fused[(M,)](x, y, w, b, mean, rstd, x.stride(0), N, eps, BLOCK_SIZE=1024)
    return y, mean, rstd


def ref_layer_norm(x, w, b, eps=1e-5):
    """Reference implementation returning output, mean, rstd."""
    out = torch.nn.functional.layer_norm(x, (x.shape[1],), w, b, eps)
    mean = x.mean(dim=1, keepdim=True)
    var = x.var(dim=1, keepdim=True, unbiased=False)
    rstd = 1 / torch.sqrt(var + eps)
    return out, mean.squeeze(1), rstd.squeeze(1)


def assert_close(a, b, msg, atol=1e-2, rtol=0):
    assert torch.allclose(a, b, atol=atol, rtol=rtol), msg


# 1. Tiny N (N=1)
torch.manual_seed(1)
x = torch.randn(4, 1)
w = torch.rand(1)
b = torch.rand(1)
out, mean, rstd = run_kernel(x, w, b)
ref_out, ref_mean, ref_rstd = ref_layer_norm(x, w, b)
assert_close(out, ref_out, "N=1 output mismatch")
assert_close(mean, ref_mean, "N=1 mean mismatch")
assert_close(rstd, ref_rstd, "N=1 rstd mismatch")

# 2. N just below BLOCK_SIZE (1023)
torch.manual_seed(2)
x = torch.randn(2, 1023)
w = torch.rand(1023)
b = torch.rand(1023)
out, mean, rstd = run_kernel(x, w, b)
ref_out, ref_mean, ref_rstd = ref_layer_norm(x, w, b)
assert_close(out, ref_out, "N=1023 output mismatch")
assert_close(mean, ref_mean, "N=1023 mean mismatch")
assert_close(rstd, ref_rstd, "N=1023 rstd mismatch")

# 3. N just above BLOCK_SIZE (1025)
torch.manual_seed(3)
x = torch.randn(2, 1025)
w = torch.rand(1025)
b = torch.rand(1025)
out, mean, rstd = run_kernel(x, w, b)
ref_out, ref_mean, ref_rstd = ref_layer_norm(x, w, b)
assert_close(out, ref_out, "N=1025 output mismatch")
assert_close(mean, ref_mean, "N=1025 mean mismatch")
assert_close(rstd, ref_rstd, "N=1025 rstd mismatch")

# 4. Extreme eps values
torch.manual_seed(4)
x = torch.randn(4, 512)
w = torch.rand(512)
b = torch.rand(512)
for eps in [1e-12, 1e-2]:
    out, mean, rstd = run_kernel(x, w, b, eps=eps)
    ref_out, ref_mean, ref_rstd = ref_layer_norm(x, w, b, eps=eps)
    assert_close(out, ref_out, f"eps={eps} output mismatch")
    assert_close(mean, ref_mean, f"eps={eps} mean mismatch")
    assert_close(rstd, ref_rstd, f"eps={eps} rstd mismatch")

# 5. Extreme magnitude values (use rtol to account for fp32 precision at large magnitudes)
torch.manual_seed(5)
for scale in [1e-4, 1e4]:
    x = scale * torch.randn(4, 256)
    w = torch.rand(256)
    b = torch.rand(256)
    out, mean, rstd = run_kernel(x, w, b)
    ref_out, ref_mean, ref_rstd = ref_layer_norm(x, w, b)
    # Relative tolerance handles precision loss at large magnitudes
    assert_close(out, ref_out, f"scale={scale} output mismatch", rtol=1e-3)
    assert_close(mean, ref_mean, f"scale={scale} mean mismatch", rtol=1e-3)
    assert_close(rstd, ref_rstd, f"scale={scale} rstd mismatch", rtol=1e-3)

# 6. Float16 dtype (kernel computes in float32, stores as float16)
torch.manual_seed(6)
x = torch.randn(4, 512, dtype=torch.float16)
w = torch.rand(512, dtype=torch.float16)
b = torch.rand(512, dtype=torch.float16)
out, mean, rstd = run_kernel(x, w, b)
ref_out, ref_mean, ref_rstd = ref_layer_norm(x.float(), w.float(), b.float())
# Compare in float32 with relaxed tolerance for fp16 storage
assert_close(out.float(), ref_out, "float16 output mismatch", atol=1e-2, rtol=1e-2)
assert_close(mean, ref_mean, "float16 mean mismatch", atol=1e-2, rtol=1e-2)
assert_close(rstd, ref_rstd, "float16 rstd mismatch", atol=1e-2, rtol=1e-2)
